trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum, and it unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are all on your account — there is nothing extra to do in the game itself. Work through this guide phase by phase: finish the story, clear every stranger strand, sample and then master the activities, sweep the map for exploration, and leave the long cumulative counters (stunts, cards, laundered cash) ticking over in the background while you play. Nothing on this list is missable, so if a trophy resists, park it and come back after the credits with better gear, more cash and a full map. When the 54th trophy pops, this one follows automatically.
trophies.tips: Leave the platinum for last; it arrives on its own once the other 54 are done.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; platinum trophy

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this trophy is simply your first step into Leonida. Start a new game and play through the introduction exactly as it unfolds: the game uses these early scenes to teach movement, driving and the basics of switching between Lucia and Jason. There are no choices to get wrong and no fail state that can lock you out — if a section goes badly, the game restarts you at a checkpoint and you try again. The trophy pops as the mission wraps up and free roam begins. There is nothing to prepare; just start the story and let it play out.
trophies.tips: Just start a new game; this is the first thing the story hands you.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; opening story mission

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Awarded automatically for finishing Chapter 1 of the main story. Follow the mission markers as they appear, completing each story job in order — the early chapter is heavily guided, introducing the map, safehouses and the core loop of taking work from contacts. You cannot wander into this one early or skip past it: chapter progress is strictly linear, and the trophy registers the moment the chapter's final mission ends. If you are unsure what to do next, check the mission list and head for the active story marker. Dying or failing a mission only costs you a checkpoint restart, never progress toward this trophy.
trophies.tips: Follow the story markers in order; chapters cannot be skipped or missed.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; main story chapter

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2 to earn this one. By now the story opens up: more of Leonida becomes reachable, new contacts start calling, and missions begin mixing driving, shooting and short on-foot sections. Keep following the main story markers in order — side content can wait, and none of it is required for the chapter to advance. The trophy pops when the chapter's closing mission is complete. A good habit from here on: keep a stocked weapon wheel and a fast car garaged, because later chapters raise the pressure. Nothing in this chapter is missable; chapter trophies simply track honest story progress.
trophies.tips: Side content can wait; chapter progress only needs the story jobs done.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; main story chapter

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3. The middle chapters are where GTA VI's story finds its stride — bigger set pieces, longer drives across the state, and missions that expect you to arrive prepared. Play the story missions in sequence and the trophy lands when the chapter closes. If a mission gives you trouble, remember the series' golden rules: use cover, let your health recover before pushing, and restock between jobs rather than saving every dollar. There are no optional objectives tied to this trophy and no way to miss it — it is a straight milestone on the road to the finale.
trophies.tips: Spend money on armour and ammo between jobs instead of hoarding it.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; main story chapter

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the endgame. Missions here are longer and less forgiving, so go in with full armour, a stocked inventory and your best weapons ready. Follow the story markers in order; the trophy registers as the chapter's final mission ends and the finale unlocks. This is also a good moment to start tidying side content — stranger strands and collectibles are all still available, and everything on the list can be finished after the credits. Nothing in Chapter 4 can be permanently missed, so push through at your own pace.
trophies.tips: After this chapter, tidy side content at leisure — it all stays open.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; main story chapter

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold trophy for completing the final story mission. It unlocks once you have finished Chapter 4, and it is the biggest set piece of the campaign — expect a long mission with several distinct phases, so start it well stocked: full armour, full ammo for your two best weapons, and health items if the game offers them. Follow the objectives as they update, use checkpoints freely, and do not be afraid to lower the difficulty in the settings if a section walls you; the trophy does not care how you finish, only that you do. When the credits roll, this gold is yours — and the whole map stays open afterwards for the 100% push.
trophies.tips: Start the finale fully stocked; difficulty settings never block the trophy.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; final story mission

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Like every named-mission trophy on this list, it is awarded for finishing that job as part of the main story — simply play through the campaign and it will come to you in order. When the mission becomes active, head to its marker and play it through; if you fail a section you restart from a checkpoint with no penalty. There is nothing optional to collect and no performance requirement — no timer to beat and no medal needed. If you are replaying from a later save, mission select after the story lets you revisit it, so it can never be permanently missed.
trophies.tips: Named-mission trophies need completion only — no medal, no timer.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; story mission

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist, one of the story's headline robbery missions. Heists in this series follow a rhythm: a setup phase, the job itself, and a heated escape, so arrive with armour, a full weapon wheel and a fast, durable getaway vehicle in mind. Play it as part of the main story and the trophy pops at the mission's end. During the escape, remember that breaking line of sight matters more than speed — duck into side streets, swap vehicles if the heat allows, and let the wanted level bleed off rather than fighting every unit. Failing any stage only restarts that checkpoint, so the trophy is never at risk.
trophies.tips: On the escape, breaking line of sight beats raw speed every time.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; story heist mission

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. This is a straight story-completion trophy: the mission arrives in sequence as you work through the campaign, and finishing it — on any difficulty, at any pace — is all that is required. Follow the objective markers, lean on checkpoints if a firefight goes wrong, and the trophy registers during the mission's closing moments. No optional collectibles, medals or side objectives are attached to it. And like everything else on this list, it stays available: mission replay after the credits covers you, so it cannot be missed for good.
trophies.tips: Pure story completion — it arrives in sequence as you play the campaign.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; story mission

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. Play the campaign in order and this mission will arrive as one of the chapter beats; finish it and the trophy is yours. Expect the usual GTA structure — travel to the marker, handle the set piece that follows, and see out any escape or tail the script calls for. There are no hidden requirements: no gold medal, no time limit and no optional objective feeds this trophy. If a section frustrates you, a checkpoint restart keeps all your progress, and lowering the difficulty in settings is always allowed. Story trophies like this one are milestones, not skill tests.
trophies.tips: A milestone, not a skill test — checkpoints keep all your progress.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; story mission

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete VCIA Takedown, a story mission centred on VCIA — Leonida's international airport, seen in Rockstar's trailers. Play through the campaign and take the mission when it activates; the trophy pops on completion. Airport jobs in this series tend to mix on-foot sections with vehicle chases on runways and perimeter roads, so keep a fast car close and your weapon wheel stocked. As with every story trophy here, there is no medal or performance condition, failure only costs a checkpoint, and the mission can be replayed after the story ends — so there is no way to lock yourself out of it.
trophies.tips: Keep a fast car close; airport jobs mix foot and vehicle sections.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; story mission at VCIA

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory, one of the later and louder story missions. The name promises a heavy operation, so prepare like it: full armour, maximum ammo, and your strongest automatic weapons ready before you start the marker. Play it as it arrives in the campaign sequence and finish every stage — the trophy registers at the mission's end. Long operations in GTA are checkpointed generously, so push forward aggressively rather than replaying whole sections after a death. Nothing about this trophy is missable or performance-based; it simply marks that you saw one of the story's biggest jobs through to the end.
trophies.tips: Go in with full armour and maximum ammo; push forward, checkpoints are generous.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; story mission

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Attain 100% completion — the checklist the game itself tracks in its stats and completion menus, and the second gold on the list. In this series, 100% means a defined subset, not literally everything: the full story, the stranger strands, a set number of activities, hobbies, collectibles and world events, all spelled out by the in-game checklist. Work it methodically after the credits: open the completion menu, pick the category with the biggest gap, and clear it before moving on. Use this guide's phases as your order of attack. It is a long road — tens of hours — but nothing on the checklist is missable, so it is purely a matter of steady, organised play.
trophies.tips: Work the in-game 100% checklist category by category after the credits.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; 100% completion checklist

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Stunts are the game's stunt jumps and similar set-piece leaps scattered across Leonida — marked challenges where a ramp, run-up and landing zone are provided, and the game tells you whether the stunt registered. Build a routine: whenever you pass one, take it, and use a fast bike or light sports car for the run-up speed most jumps need. Failed attempts cost nothing — turn around and go again. The counter is cumulative across your whole save, so progress made while exploring counts. Keep a note of areas you have cleared so late-game mop-up is a short tour rather than a fresh search of the whole state.
trophies.tips: Take every stunt you pass during normal play; mop-up is a short tour.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stunt challenges

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once. Leonida is full of side activities — races, shooting ranges, fishing, arcade games, drone events and more — and this trophy simply asks you to sample every category a single time. You do not need to win, score, or even finish well: starting each activity once is enough. The natural way to earn it is curiosity — whenever a new activity icon appears on your map, go and try it instead of driving past. If you reach the endgame unsure what is missing, compare the activities listed in the stats menu against the icons on your map; the one you have never touched is your answer.
trophies.tips: Never drive past a new activity icon — sampling it once is the whole job.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; side activities

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges. Visit the shooting range, work through its challenge list — typically accuracy, speed and target-variety drills with different weapon classes — and hit the gold score in each. Start with the weapons you handle best to learn the scoring, then mop up the rest. Practical tips that always apply in this series: control your fire in short bursts, prioritise the targets worth the most points, reload during lulls rather than mid-combo, and replay a challenge immediately while the layout is fresh. Medals are permanent once earned, so progress is never lost — grind one challenge at a time until the set is gold.
trophies.tips: Replay a challenge immediately while its layout is fresh in your hands.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; shooting range challenges

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location. Top Fun events are drone time-trials: a course of gates or checkpoints laid out around a location, flown against the clock or rival drones. Find each event marker on the map, learn the course on a first exploratory run, then push for the win once you know the tight corners and the best line. Drone handling rewards smoothness over aggression — small early corrections beat late swerves. You must win at every location, not just one, so keep a note of the sites you have cleared. Wins are permanent, and events can be retried immediately, making this a pure practice trophy.
trophies.tips: Learn each course on a slow first run, then push for the win.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; Top Fun drone races

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Leonida offers racing in several flavours — street races, off-road events, and water or air events depending on what the map provides — and the key word is different: winning the same race twenty times does not count. Tour the map and enter every unique race you find, using a vehicle suited to the class; upgrading your regular cars pays off here. Early races are forgiving while you learn, and race events can be retried straight away after a loss. Track your distinct wins in the stats menu. Twenty unique victories sounds like a lot, but spread across the story hours it arrives almost on its own.
trophies.tips: The word that matters is 'different' — tour the map instead of farming one race.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; races

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is one of the contacts you meet around Leonida's waters, and his challenge is a head-to-head fishing contest: fish against him under the challenge rules and out-score his haul. Learn the basics at any fishing spot first — how casting, hooking and reeling behave, and which spots the game favours — then take the challenge once the mechanics feel natural. Fishing systems in this series reward patience: watch for the bite, strike on time, and manage line tension rather than reeling flat-out. If you lose, the challenge can be retried; Cal is not going anywhere, and neither is this trophy.
trophies.tips: Practise at a free fishing spot first; patience beats fast reeling.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; fishing challenge with Cal

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete an arcade game. Find an arcade cabinet — arcades and bars across Leonida stock playable machines — walk up, and play one of its games through to completion. 'Complete' means finishing a full game session rather than quitting at the title screen, so pick the machine whose game looks shortest or most familiar if you want this quickly. These cabinets are flavour content: cheap to play, quick to finish, and a nice break between missions. This is one of the simplest bronzes on the list and can be earned the first time you wander into an arcade, so grab it early and forget about it.
trophies.tips: Pick the shortest-looking cabinet game and play one full session.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; arcade games

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy — that means finishing Andy's whole stranger strand, not just meeting him. Stranger strands work like this: a character appears on the map with their marker, you take their first job, and after each job the strand advances until a final mission closes their story. Do every Andy job as it appears, waiting for the follow-up calls or markers between stages — strands often unlock in steps tied to story progress or time passing in-game. When the strand's last mission ends, the trophy pops. Andy's strand is one of the eight that also feed the Strangers & Freaks silver.
trophies.tips: One meeting is not enough — only the strand's final mission counts.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger strand (Andy)

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton by finishing his entire stranger strand. Find Kenton's marker on the map, take his first job, and keep returning as new stages open — strands advance step by step, and the next stage sometimes needs a day or two of in-game time, or further story progress, before it appears. The trophy is awarded only when the strand's concluding mission is done, so a single meeting is not enough. If Kenton's marker vanishes mid-strand, do not panic: progress further in the story or let time pass and check the map again. Finishing Kenton also counts toward the eight strands needed for Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.tips: If the marker vanishes, advance the story or let in-game days pass.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger strand (Kenton)

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy by seeing his stranger strand through to its end. Billy's jobs appear under his map marker as a connected chain: finish one stage and the next unlocks after some time passes or the story moves on. Work the chain whenever his marker is live and the trophy pops at the end of his final job. Stranger strands are never missable in this series — the characters wait for you — so if Billy goes quiet, advance the main story and look again. His strand is also one of the eight that count toward the Strangers & Freaks silver, so finishing him pays twice.
trophies.tips: Strands pause, they never cancel — Billy waits for you after the credits too.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger strand (Billy)

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida. Strangers are the side characters marked on your map whose short story chains sit outside the main campaign — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have a named trophy for finishing their strand, and this silver asks for eight full strands in total. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so half-finished chains do not help. Method: whenever a stranger marker appears, prioritise it, and between stages let in-game time pass or advance the story to trigger the next step. Clear all five named strands first, then hunt the remaining three among the other markers on the map.
trophies.tips: Clear the five named strands first, then find three more markers.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger strands

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy by finishing his full stranger strand. Randy's marker appears on the map like the other strangers; take his first job, then keep an eye out for the follow-ups — each completed stage schedules the next, sometimes after a delay or a story milestone. The trophy lands only when the strand's last mission is complete. Stranger content in GTA is built to wait for you: nothing here expires, and Randy will still be there after the credits, so there is no pressure to rush his chain early. His finished strand also counts as one of the eight needed for the Strangers & Freaks silver.
trophies.tips: No expiry and no rush — strands are still there after the credits.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger strand (Randy)

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone, closing out his stranger strand. Find Tyrone's marker, work his first job, and keep returning as the chain advances — strand stages unlock one at a time, often after in-game time passes or you finish other missions in between. Only the final mission of the strand triggers the trophy, so see it all the way through. If his marker is missing for a while, progress the story and check again; strands pause, they never cancel. Tyrone's strand is one of the five with its own trophy and one of the eight that build toward the Strangers & Freaks silver, so it is doubly worth finishing.
trophies.tips: See the chain all the way through; only the final mission pops it.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; stranger strand (Tyrone)

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet, scenic locations marked out in the world — find one, use the prompt, and the game runs a short meditation moment. The trophy needs every spot, so this is a collector's tour of the state's prettiest corners. Work region by region so you never criss-cross the map, and combine the sweep with other exploration trophies — vehicle discoveries and map completion fill in as you travel. If the stats menu tracks the count, check it before the final push so you know how many remain. None of the spots are missable; they wait exactly where they are.
trophies.tips: Sweep region by region and stack this with map exploration.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; meditation spots

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret is a hunting contact, and his strand leads to a unique animal — a one-of-a-kind specimen rather than the common wildlife roaming Leonida. Take Bret's hunting jobs as they appear and follow his directions: tracking in this series means moving slowly, watching for signs and taking a clean shot when the animal shows itself. Prepare with a suitable long-range weapon and whatever hunting aids the game provides. Because the animal is unique, follow the mission structure rather than free-hunting at random — the encounter is staged through Bret's jobs. If a hunt goes wrong, retry the stage.
trophies.tips: Follow Bret's staged hunt rather than free-hunting at random.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; hunting for Bret

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 Collectible Card sets. Leonida hides collectible cards across the map, grouped into sets — finish any three full sets. Cards sit in the kinds of places this series loves: rooftops, alleys, interiors, lookout points and the far ends of piers, so thorough exploration is the real requirement. Play with an eye on your surroundings; collectibles often reward a second look at somewhere you have already been. Track set progress in the collections menu so you know which sets are nearly done, and close those first. Every card is available from the start of free roam and stays there after the story — nothing is missable; it is purely a long, satisfying sweep.
trophies.tips: Close the nearly-finished sets first; check the collections menu.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; collectible card sets

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK is one of Leonida's in-world brands with interactive spots spread across the state — when you find one, use it, and the counter climbs. One hundred locations is a grind by design, and the trick is to make it ambient: whenever you spot a WAiNK location during normal play, stop for the few seconds it takes rather than planning a dedicated hundred-stop tour at the end. Combine the hunt with exploration and collectible routes so the stops stack. The counter is cumulative and permanent, and nothing about it is missable — it is a marathon that rewards players who start early.
trophies.tips: Start on day one and make it ambient, not a hundred-stop endgame tour.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; WAiNK locations

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 Challenges. Challenges are the game's structured side objectives — the tracked tasks the menus group under challenges, ranging from combat and driving feats to activity milestones. Fifty is a big number, but most challenges are designed to complete through ordinary play if you vary what you do: mix up weapons, vehicles and activities instead of repeating one loop. Check the challenges menu regularly, pick out the ones sitting nearly finished, and close them deliberately — that habit turns a vague grind into a checklist. Progress is cumulative across your whole save, challenges never reset, and there is no deadline: steady variety gets you there.
trophies.tips: Regularly close the nearly-finished challenges instead of grinding blind.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; challenges menu

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat. You need Lucia and Jason together — the game's partner system — when the escape happens: build a four-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear. Open ground will not work; use the series' classic tools — alleys, tunnels, parking structures, off-road cuts and a vehicle swap when the search turns cold. The important detail is that your partner must be present for the escape, so set it up deliberately in free roam rather than hoping a story mission arranges it. Raising four stars is easy: cause serious mayhem, then run smart.
trophies.tips: Set it up deliberately in free roam with your partner already beside you.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; partner wanted-level escape

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level. Bring your partner along in free roam, pick a cluster of shops close together, and rob them in one continuous run: threaten the clerk, take the register money, and move straight to the next shop while the wanted level from the first robbery is still active. The chain breaks if your wanted level fully clears, so keep moving and do not hide long enough to go clean between shops. A fast car waiting outside each time keeps the run smooth. If the chain breaks, no harm done — shops reset, so pick another cluster and start again with your partner beside you.
trophies.tips: Choose a tight cluster of shops and never let the stars fully clear mid-run.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; partner shop robberies

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. A vehicle counts as discovered the first time you get in and drive it, so this trophy rewards variety: every time you see a car, bike, boat or aircraft you have not used, take it for a spin before carrying on. Traffic variety changes by district and time of day — rich areas, docks, farms and airfields all spawn different pools — so regular map-wide travel fills the counter naturally. Deliberate mop-up is easy too: walk a few busy streets and parking areas and sample everything parked. One hundred sounds like a grind, but across a full playthrough most players pass it without trying; check the vehicle stats to watch the number climb.
trophies.tips: Sample every new vehicle you see; district variety does the rest.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; vehicle discovery

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-motion aiming ability — one activation gives you a short window, and five enemies must fall inside it. Set the moment up rather than hoping for it: find a spot where a group clusters — a gang hangout, a roadblock, or a mission ambush — top up the ability, position yourself with a clear view, then trigger it with a high-capacity automatic weapon and sweep target to target. Headshots drop enemies fastest, buying time for the fifth. If you land four, do not force it; refill the ability and stage a bigger group. It is a setup trophy, not a reflex trophy.
trophies.tips: Stage a clustered group first — this is a setup trophy, not a reflex trophy.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; Combat Focus ability

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA. VCIA is Leonida's international airport — the one from Rockstar's trailers — and an 'unscheduled departure' means getting airborne in a plane you were never cleared to take: enter the airfield, find a usable aircraft, and take off while the authorities object. Expect an instant wanted level, so work fast once you commit — line up on a runway or taxiway with a clear run and get wheels-up before the response boxes you in. The trophy should register as the departure happens. Airfield security is the whole challenge here; the flying itself is the easy part. If you get wasted or busted, walk back in and try again.
trophies.tips: Commit fast once inside the fence; the takeoff run must be clear.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; VCIA airport (Rockstar trailers)

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is the whole hint: 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos.' A Rhino is the series' name for its battle tank, and this trophy is earned by getting into one and doing what tanks do — expect it to involve taking a Rhino on a destructive run until the trophy registers. Rhinos live where the military keeps them, so this one likely waits until you can reach a base or until the story puts armour on the field; breaking into a military installation means instant heavy resistance, so go in fast, get to the tank, and let its armour do the talking once you are inside. Exact conditions confirm against the shipped game; a Rhino plus heat means a rampage.
trophies.tips: Get to the tank fast; once you are inside, its armour does the talking.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; exact trigger confirmed against the shipped game

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. This is the stealth counterpart to the smash-and-grab robberies: pick a jewelry store, go in prepared to stay unseen, and get the goods out without detection ever being raised. Learn the store first — where the staff are, and which exit gives you a clean line away. Move slowly, use whatever stealth tools the game gives you, and if a robbery option lets you threaten quietly rather than loudly, take it. Being spotted mid-job voids the attempt but nothing else: leave, let things cool down, and try another store or the same one later. Patience, not firepower, earns this one.
trophies.tips: Scout the store and your exit line before you ever make a move.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; jewelry store robbery

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 Bank Vaults and escape. Bank vault robberies are the heavyweight scores of free roam: find a bank with an accessible vault, get in, clear the vault, and then complete the part that actually earns the trophy — the escape. Losing the heat afterwards is the real test, so plan your exit before you go in: a fast vehicle staged outside, a route that breaks line of sight quickly, and ideally a change of vehicle once the search cools. Each successful vault-and-escape counts once, so work five jobs methodically rather than repeating chaos. Progress is permanent per escape, and banks reset over time, so this is very doable in a few focused sessions.
trophies.tips: Plan the escape before you enter; the getaway is the real test.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; bank vault robberies

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an Armored Truck and escape. Armored trucks patrol Leonida's roads carrying cash; the classic blitz play, named for the series' famous armoured-truck ambushes, is to stop one hard and fast — block it, deal with its guards and doors, take the money, and then outrun the wanted level that follows. Rear doors on these trucks are built to resist, so bring serious firepower or explosives if the game offers them. Once the cash is yours, the escape is standard craft: break line of sight, swap vehicles, wait out the search. Trucks respawn endlessly on the roads, so failed attempts cost nothing — another one is always a few minutes away.
trophies.tips: Bring heavy firepower for the rear doors; trucks respawn endlessly.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; armored truck robbery

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida. The map tracks revealed territory: as you travel, the fog lifts district by district, and this trophy needs the whole state uncovered — every city block, swamp road, key and coastal corner. It sounds enormous, but story missions and side content carry you across most of it naturally; the real work is the quiet corners no mission visits. Late-game mop-up is a road trip: take an aircraft or fast car, open the map, and head for every patch still fogged, working the edges and islands systematically. Exploration progress is permanent, so every trip counts. Pair this sweep with meditation spots and collectibles to make the miles pay twice.
trophies.tips: Save the mop-up for a fast aircraft and work the fogged edges systematically.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; map exploration

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang. Leonida's gangs each run illegal operations — businesses and rackets on their turf — and this trophy wants you to hit at least one belonging to every gang in the state. As you play, note which gangs you have encountered and where their operations sit; gang presence becomes clearer as the story and side content introduce each crew. When you rob an operation, expect armed resistance rather than a frightened clerk, so arrive stocked and plan the exit. One robbery per gang is enough — you are sending a message, not dismantling anyone. Keep a simple tally so the last gang on the list is a deliberate trip, not a guessing game.
trophies.tips: Keep a written tally of gangs hit; one operation per gang is enough.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; gang operations

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Ocean Beach is the famous strip on Vice Beach's oceanfront — the neon shoreline from every trailer. Somewhere along it is a spot where you can enjoy a cocktail and take in the view; find a bar or the right interaction prompt on the beachfront, use it, and let the moment play out. This is one of the list's gentle trophies — a deliberate pause to admire the scenery the developers built. The exact spot confirms against the shipped game, but the shape of it is simple: go to Ocean Beach, find the cocktail prompt, and drink in the view. A two-minute trophy, best earned at sunset.
trophies.tips: Head to the Ocean Beach front and look for the cocktail interaction prompt.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; Ocean Beach (Rockstar trailers)

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. Find a vehicle showroom — a dealership with a glass front and cars on display — get inside a display vehicle, and drive it straight out through the showroom glass. 'In classic style' is the series' wink at one of its most famous mission openings, and the recipe is the same: car, accelerator, window. The trophy should pop as you make your exit. Expect a wanted level for the trouble, so have a route away in mind, though nothing about the escape is required — the smash itself is the trophy. If one showroom does not cooperate, Leonida has more than one place that sells cars behind glass.
trophies.tips: Car, accelerator, window — the smash itself is the whole trophy.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; vehicle showroom escape

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Kolt & Associates is one of Leonida's in-world firms, and its bowling alley is a playable activity venue: go there, start a game of bowling, and play — the 'follow-through' wording points at actually bowling properly rather than just visiting. Learn the alley's throwing mechanic on your first frames, then settle in and finish what the game asks of a visit. Bowling alleys in this series are social venues, so you may find the activity opens through the map marker like other pastimes. This is a light, quick bronze: one visit, one game, done — and it also ticks bowling off your Master of None activity sampler.
trophies.tips: One visit, one game — and it counts toward Master of None too.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; Kolt & Associates bowling alley

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The description reads 'A partnership with mass appeal' — a partner trophy about Lucia and Jason together, and one of the list's deliberately vague ones. Trophies worded like this in the series usually attach to a shared activity or a moment the two protagonists do together, so the practical approach is breadth: use the partner system often, take your partner along for activities, hangouts and jobs, and let the shared content accumulate. The exact trigger confirms against the shipped game and its in-game description, which wins if it differs. Nothing partner-related is missable, so keep playing together and this one resolves itself.
trophies.tips: Use the partner system often and let shared content accumulate.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; exact trigger confirmed against the shipped game

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: The description says 'Choices made (for better or worse)' — a trophy tied to the decisions the story puts in front of you. GTA VI's campaign gives Lucia and Jason moments where your choice shapes what follows, and this trophy registers that a meaningful choice has been made and lived with. There is no wrong answer to hunt for: play the story naturally, commit to the choices you make rather than reloading to shop for outcomes, and the trophy follows from the narrative itself. Because it hangs off story decisions, it cannot be forced early. The exact trigger confirms against the shipped game.
trophies.tips: Commit to your choices instead of reloading to shop for outcomes.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; story choices

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: The description reads 'Second time's the charm' — the list's shrug in trophy form. Wording like this usually marks a fail-and-retry moment: something that goes wrong the first time and works when you come back to it, whether that is a specific encounter, vehicle or attempt the game stages for you. Play naturally and do not rage-reload at the first disaster; if the game hands you a scripted misfortune, roll with it and take the second attempt it offers. The precise trigger confirms against the shipped game and its in-game wording, which wins if it differs. It is not missable — it is attached to playing through, not to playing perfectly.
trophies.tips: Do not reload at the first disaster — take the second attempt offered.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; exact trigger confirmed against the shipped game

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: The description asks 'What the hell just happened?' — this is the list's weird-encounter trophy, Leonida's nod to the series' long tradition of strange happenings in remote places: odd lights, stranger events and things the game never quite explains. Trophies like this are found by exploring the far corners — the swamps, the keys and the empty night roads — and by investigating anything that looks deliberately out of place. If something uncanny happens while you roam, follow it rather than driving on. The exact event confirms against the shipped game; treat this guide's job as pointing you at the unknown rather than spoiling it. Keep your eyes open out there.
trophies.tips: Investigate anything out of place in the far corners of the map.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; exact event confirmed against the shipped game

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by. A melee drive-by means striking people from a moving vehicle with a melee attack rather than a gun — lean out, swing, and knock down your targets like pins. You need a vehicle that allows it and a group of pedestrians or enemies positioned close to your line: drive along a pavement edge or through a clustered group at moderate speed — too fast and you cannot connect, too slow and it is just a collision. Line up several targets in one pass for the full ten-pin flavour. Practise somewhere quiet first; once the timing clicks, it is a thirty-second trophy. Being caught mid-attempt costs nothing but a wanted level you can shed.
trophies.tips: Moderate speed is everything — too fast whiffs, too slow just collides.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; melee drive-by

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are hot money — takings that cannot be spent until a contact cleans them — and this trophy tracks the cumulative total you push through the laundering pipeline. Build the habit early: whenever you hold marked bills from robberies and scores, route them to your laundering contacts instead of letting them sit, and keep a steady flow of income-generating crime feeding the top. The counter is cumulative across your whole save, so every batch counts and nothing is wasted. A quarter of a million is a long-game target by design; treat it as a background meter that fills while you play the rest of the list.
trophies.tips: Launder every batch as it comes in; never let marked bills sit.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; money laundering contacts

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Every legitimate purchase counts toward the total — clothes, weapons, ammo, vehicle work, food, services — anywhere the game takes your money at a till. There is no trick to it and no reason to save for it specially: a full playthrough of GTA spends this naturally many times over, especially once vehicle upgrades and property costs arrive. If you want it early, outfitting both protagonists properly — wardrobes, weapon sets, a tuned car each — burns a healthy chunk in one session. The counter is cumulative and permanent, and spending is what the money is for: this trophy is the game paying you to enjoy yourself.
trophies.tips: Outfit both protagonists fully and this lands almost by itself.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; shop spending

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties. Across Leonida, properties with garages come up for sale — buy every one of them. This is fundamentally a money trophy: the garages themselves are straightforward purchases, but affording the full set means building serious income first through story payouts, robberies and side work. Check property listings as they unlock — new properties surface as the story opens new areas — and buy steadily rather than saving for one giant spree at the end. Each purchase is permanent and expands your vehicle storage. If one property seems missing, progress the story; the full set only lists once every district is open to you.
trophies.tips: Buy steadily as districts open; a 'missing' garage means more story first.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; garage properties

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is one of Leonida's in-world services, and its app lets you register vehicles — when you are in a vehicle you want on your list, use the app or its registration option and add it. Ten registrations is quick once you know the mechanic exists: register your story cars, your favourites and a few street finds until the counter fills. The deliberate approach is to register each genuinely new vehicle you keep rather than hunting ten throwaway cars at the end. Registrations are permanent, the vehicles you register become easier to recover and use, and the whole thing takes minutes once the habit forms.
trophies.tips: Register each keeper vehicle as you acquire it; the habit fills the counter.
trophies.source: Official trophy list; Scooter Bros app
